messages:
renee: quick flag from onboarding: nebula-xt4q (FP32 -> PTQ int8) failing structured-tool contracts at ~3.9% vs float32 0.7% on the same eval set.

arjun: thanks. streaming or whole-response parse?

renee: whole-response. Parser errors cluster as: 1) truncated arrays (missing closing brackets), 2) numeric fields turned into strings, 3) occasional stray backslashes inside strings.

maya: can you paste a raw example?

renee: raw output example below (copied from the log):
```
{"request_id":"c9f2","actions":[{"type":"pick","options":"[\"red\",\"blue\"]"}],"result_count":null}
```

arjun: ugh attributes/options serialized-as-string again. looks like model emitted a literal \"[\" at token boundaries. any temp/sampling signal?

renee: yes. temp=0.8 -> 5.8% failures. temp=0.0 -> 1.9% for int8. float32 stays ~0.7 across temps. top_p didn't change much.

bench-bot: run-summary: nebula-xt4q-int8-2026-03-21 sample=6k structured_fail=3.9% median_latency=210ms

maya: short prompts (<80 tokens) disproportionately affected. hypothesis: early EOS or tokenization boundary leads to partial array emission. quantization amplifies subword split instability.

arjun: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) response postprocessor heuristic to coerce quoted JSON arrays back into arrays, replace null numeric fields with 0 or empty list per schema, 2) temporarily lower onboard int8 canary temp to 0.0, 3) add an opt-in regen-on-parse-fail path that retries with greedy sampling.

renee: started a tiny canary: nebula-int8-safe -> temp=0.0, regen_on_fail=true, postrepair=true. rolling 50k requests.

ops-bot: deploy note: nebula-int8-safe canary started at 6161617035 target=50k processed=1.1k failures=2.2%

maya: long-term: add a structured-output stress suite that sweeps quant levels, temps, and tokenizer boundaries; record per-field dropout and serialization errors. we should also check kernel export flags for PTQ build; some quant kernels may change token-emission behavior.

arjun: agree. renee, can you open a short RFC with bench plan + quick checklist for kernel sanity? tag me and bench-bot.

renee: will draft RFC today and open PR for postrepair hook. will post canary logs to the run link when available.

arjun: cool. if failures don't drop under 1% with canary, escalate to model-teams for re-run with different calibration or mixed-precision fallback. :thumbsup:
